claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
**I'm sorry, but you are not eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:

**The key issue:** Another claimant who lives with Alex has priority over your claim. According to UK Child Benefit rules, only one person can get Child Benefit for a child at a time. Since another person living with Alex already has priority, you cannot claim Child Benefit for them.

**Other factors in your situation:**
- **Age and education:** Alex is 19 and in approved education, which would normally allow Child Benefit to continue until age 20
- **Work hours:** Although Alex works 24+ hours per week, this doesn't automatically disqualify them since they remain in approved education
- **Hospital stay:** Alex has been in hospital for 11 weeks, which is just under the 12-week threshold where Child Benefit normally stops

However, all of these factors are secondary to the main issue: **the other claimant who lives with Alex has the priority claim**.

If you believe you should be the claimant instead, you would need to agree this with the other person, or HMRC would need to decide between you. The other person would need to contact the Child Benefit Office to stop their claim before you could make a new claim.

However, there is a critical issue: another claimant who lives with the child has priority. According to the guidance, 'Only one person can get Child Benefit for a child,' and 'If you and someone else are responsible for the same child, agree between yourselves who will get Child Benefit. If you cannot agree, HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) will decide who will get it.' Since another claimant living with Alex has priority, you would not be eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex - the other person with priority would be the eligible claimant. Additionally, while Alex works 24+ hours per week, this would normally disqualify them unless they remain in approved education or training - which they are, so this aspect doesn't disqualify them. The fact that Alex has been in hospital for 11 weeks is also relevant, as Child Benefit normally stops after 12 weeks in hospital unless exceptions apply (such as regularly spending money on them), but this is secondary to the primary issue that another claimant has priority. Alex does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right, is not in local authority care, is not fostered, and has not started an apprenticeship in England - none of which would disqualify them on their own.
